quality_assessment: Excellent chapter with comprehensive coverage of advanced regex features. All major features are accurately documented with correct syntax and practical examples. Only minor improvements suggested.

issues.description: Chapter doesn't explicitly mention that \p{Emoji} may not be fully supported or may behave differently across regex engines
issues.should_add: Note about emoji matching reliability and potential differences between regex engines
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a note in the Unicode Patterns section mentioning that emoji matching may vary, and users should test patterns with their specific use case
issues.source_reference: No test coverage found for \p{Emoji} patterns in tests/

issues.description: Chapter doesn't explain what 'JIT: enabled' means in --pcre2-version output
issues.should_be: Explain that JIT (Just-In-Time compilation) improves PCRE2 performance significantly
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a brief explanation that JIT compilation provides significant performance improvement for PCRE2 patterns

issues.description: Could be clearer about when PCRE2 is 'generally slower' - it's specifically due to backtracking vs DFA
issues.current_content:
Generally slower than default engine:
- Backtracking regex implementation vs finite automata
issues.should_be: Add explanation that backtracking can cause exponential behavior on pathological patterns
issues.fix_suggestion: Expand the PCRE2 performance section to mention potential exponential time complexity with backtracking and suggest testing on representative data

issues.description: Missing advice about when you might legitimately need to increase regex limits
issues.should_add: Explain common scenarios where limits are hit (auto-generated patterns, large alternations) vs when the pattern should be simplified
issues.fix_suggestion: Add subsection 'When to Increase Limits vs Simplify' with guidance on distinguishing legitimate complex patterns from poorly designed ones

positive_aspects: Comprehensive coverage of all major advanced regex features
Correct documentation of --engine flag with all three options (default, pcre2, auto)
Clear explanation of multiline mode memory implications
Accurate comparison table of Default vs PCRE2 features
Good coverage of lookaround assertions with correct syntax
Helpful decision tree at the end
Well-organized with clear table of contents
Good balance of explanation and examples
Proper explanation of regex size limits and DFA limits
Excellent 'Limitations and Gotchas' section addressing common mistakes
improvement_suggestions: Add a brief mention of PCRE2 JIT compilation benefits in the PCRE2 section
Consider adding a note about emoji matching reliability
Expand the performance section with more details on backtracking complexity
Add guidance on when to increase regex limits vs simplify patterns
Consider adding a 'Testing Your Patterns' subsection with tips on using --debug and --stats
Could add more examples of problematic patterns that hit regex limits
Consider adding a cross-reference to the Troubleshooting chapter for regex errors
